Daginnus, K., Marty, T., Trotta, N.V., Brinkmann, T., Whitfield, A. and Roudier, S. (2023). Best Available Techniques (BAT) Reference Document for Common Waste Gas Management and Treatment Systems in the Chemical Sector. Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU (Integrated Pollution Prevention and Control). JRC Science for Policy Report JRC131915, EUR 31393 EN. Luxembourg: Publications Office of the European Union. ISBN 978-92-76-61947-5, doi:10.2760/220326.

Targeted pass of a 392-page BREF (printed page = PDF page - 28 throughout). Locators are PRINTED page numbers. The document is about non-GHG air pollutants (VOC, dust, NOx, CO, inorganic gases); it states that GHGs other than N2O are outside its scope, and it gives NO N2O abatement techniques, NO flare section (the word flare does not occur), no emerging techniques (Ch.5 empty) and almost no energy or cost data (economics sections say only relatively expensive / no information provided). Loaded (main file): thermal oxidation (straight, recuperative, regenerative) and catalytic oxidation - description, typical operating temperature range, and waste-gas flow per emission point (Tables 3.10, 3.11: median as value, min/max as range, percentiles in note); off-gas combustion in gas engines/boilers (description only). Measures: LDAR (>90% fugitive VOC reduction, EUR 60 000 per monitoring cycle at one plant). Other-values: E-PRTR N2O total for the chemical industry, VOC removal efficiencies, process furnace/heater thermal-input distribution and temperature range, OGI camera and VOC analyser prices. Not loaded: BAT-AELs and emission-level scatter plots (non-GHG; charts), SCR/SNCR NOx removal, absorption/adsorption/filters/ESP (no energy or cost numbers), polymer and viscose specific loads (VOC/CS2/H2S per t product). The triage targets (N2O abatement %, oxidiser energy use and cost, flare minimisation) are not in this document; for N2O see the LVIC-AAF and LVOC BREFs.
